key_insight: A four-wave-plate polarization compensator plus an eight-Stokes reconstruction protocol enables broadband, non-universal-safe compensation of link-induced polarization rotations even when the controller sits between two optical channel segments.
engineering_relevance: This improves practical quantum optical links by allowing flexible compensator placement, wavelength-aware polarization control, and low-error operation across temperature drift in wavelength-division-multiplexed systems.
method: Use a four-wave-plate sequence to synthesize arbitrary SO(3) polarization transformations over a broad wavelength range.
Reconstruct the two channel-segment Mueller matrices on either side of the compensator with an eight-Stokes vector protocol.
Select auxiliary wavelengths to track drift without interrupting quantum communication.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports sub-percent excess QBER more than 100 nm from the design wavelength and below 1% while tracking temperature-driven drift with two auxiliary wavelengths.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate segment-wise reconstruction and wavelength calibration, and residual controller non-idealities may still limit operation in strongly wavelength-sensitive links.
paper_title: Broadband Polarization Compensation with Link Segment Reconstruction for Quantum Optical Links
